en.html:
Kanae's voice was perfectly carefree. Nothing of the other day seemed to be troubling it.
My own mind could not perform this service.

One memory pulled another after it. The seeds of anguish were ready to sprout again.
Somehow I pressed them down. In their place, exhaustion settled on both shoulders with the weight of stone.

Carefully, I kept the sarcasm out of that answer.
Since that day, the Ootori pair had left their rooms at the Chief's house empty. We had not met. For my peace of mind, this absence had been a positive contribution.

Honestly, a few more days without meeting would have suited me very well.

But depending on the Captain's business, perhaps that much peace was also not available...

en.html:
Captain Ootori let the word trail off.
Her voice had been converted into an electrical signal. The hesitation had survived the journey perfectly.

People recognized the telephone's usefulness, but it was still far from common.
Getting one installed was expensive. Using it was also expensive. The expense had made arrangements at both ends.

Captain Ootori did not appear short of money. I could hardly imagine the cost troubling her.
Still, this was the first time she had called me. Usually, if there was business, she told me to my face.

For not doing that now, there ought to be some reason.

やや、言葉尻を濁す大鳥大尉。
　逡巡の様子は、音声の信号化を経ても消えず残って
伝わってきていた。

　電話はその利便性を認められながらも、まだ一般へ
の普及が進んでいるとは言えない機器だ。
　設置コストは高くつき、利用料金もまた同様である。

　経済的に困窮しているようには見えない大鳥大尉に
とってそれが重要な問題たるとは考えられなかったが、
電話を使って連絡を取ってきたのは今が初めてだった。
　彼女は大概、用があれば口頭で伝えてくる。

　今回そうしないからには、理由がある筈だ。

Kenchouji, on Kofukusan, ranked first among the temples called the Five Mountains of Kamakura.
An old Zen temple, founded by Tokiyori Houjou, fifth regent of the Kamakura Shogunate.
Rinzai school.

One of Kamakura's principal temples, so naturally I had visited.
Visited. That was the full extent of our relationship.
Why I must rush there now, I could not imagine.

Whatever was happening at Kenchouji ought to be a matter far removed from me.

en.html: I nodded at her words. In one place, the intonation had been peculiar. If I remembered correctly, the news had come a day or two after the sword-offering visit to Hachimangu. ...That did not prove there was no connection between Moriuji Ashikaga's sudden death and the Prince.◆ Now only this thought arrived. Perhaps the Prince had found an assassin to replace me and gone ahead. If the Lord General was killed during the visit, that was hardly something to announce without care. Wait a little, then report a mere 'sudden death'—no contradiction there. I had not seen it myself, but apparently Hachimangu had been tightly sealed since the visit. For what reason, unknown. ...Enough to feed the suspicion. A possibility only, though. One possibility. Some convenient assassin sitting ready beside the Prince—that was difficult to imagine. Thinking this far, I finally noticed that I had stopped speaking.

If I remembered correctly, the news had come a day or two after the sword-offering visit to Hachimangu.

...That did not prove there was no connection between Moriuji Ashikaga's sudden death and the Prince.◆

Now only this thought arrived.

Perhaps the Prince had found an assassin to replace me and gone ahead. If the Lord General was killed during the visit, that was hardly something to announce without care. Wait a little, then report a mere 'sudden death'—no contradiction there.

I had not seen it myself, but apparently Hachimangu had been tightly sealed since the visit. For what reason, unknown.
...Enough to feed the suspicion.

A possibility only, though. One possibility.
Some convenient assassin sitting ready beside the Prince—that was difficult to imagine.
Thinking this far, I finally noticed that I had stopped speaking.

en.html:
She cut the call.
I glared at the receiver. Now it had only a meaningless signal to offer. I put it back in its cradle.

...What was this?
The Prince was going to be attacked? Because some scheme had failed?

So it had been the Prince who sent the Lord General to the underworld? Rokuhara had found out, and now this was retaliation?
Or was the matter not so simple—

No.
This was no time to sit making guesses about what went on behind it.

If everything the Captain said was true, then her last advice was correct also.
Action. Now.
